chapters.title: Visions of God by the River
chapters.synopsis: Among the captives by the river of Chebar in Babylon, Ezekiel sees the heavens opened. Four living creatures, wheels within wheels full of eyes, and a throne bearing the likeness of the glory of the Lord appear in a whirlwind of fire.

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: Ezekiel dates his vision among the captives

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: Living creatures, wheels, and the throne of glory

chapters.title: Sent to a Rebellious House
chapters.synopsis: The Lord sets Ezekiel on his feet and commissions him as a prophet to the rebellious house of Israel. Whether they hear or refuse, they will know a prophet has been among them, and a hand offers him a scroll written with lamentations and woe.

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: The Spirit sets Ezekiel on his feet

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Commission to rebellious Israel; the written roll

chapters.title: A Watchman unto Israel
chapters.synopsis: Ezekiel eats the scroll, which is sweet as honey, and is carried to the captives at Tel-abib. The Lord appoints him a watchman to warn the wicked, making him accountable for the blood of those he fails to warn, then binds his tongue until God opens his mouth.

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: Eating the roll; carried to Tel-abib

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The watchman's charge and accountability

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: The glory appears again; silence imposed

chapters.title: The Siege Portrayed on a Tile
chapters.synopsis: Ezekiel is told to engrave Jerusalem on a tile and act out its siege, lying on his side to bear the iniquity of Israel and Judah for appointed days. Scant rationed bread and water dramatize the famine coming upon the besieged city.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Sign of the tile: Jerusalem besieged

chapters.title: The Sign of the Sharp Razor
chapters.synopsis: Ezekiel shaves his head and beard and divides the hair into thirds, burned, smitten, and scattered, a sign of how Jerusalem's people will fall by famine, sword, and dispersion. Because the city rebelled against God's judgments more than the nations around her, judgment will be executed in the sight of all.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The divided hair as a sign

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Jerusalem judged before the nations

chapters.title: Judgment on the High Places
chapters.synopsis: Ezekiel prophesies against the mountains of Israel, where altars and idols will be broken and the slain will fall before their images. Yet a remnant scattered among the nations will remember the Lord and know that he is God.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Idolatrous high places destroyed; a remnant spared

chapters.title: An End Is Come
chapters.synopsis: The Lord declares that an end has come upon the four corners of the land of Israel; the day of trouble is near. Silver and gold cannot deliver in the day of wrath, and the people will know that the Lord smites.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The day of the Lord's wrath is near

chapters.title: Abominations in the Temple
chapters.synopsis: Carried in vision from Babylon to Jerusalem, Ezekiel is shown the image of jealousy, elders burning incense to idols in dark chambers, women weeping for Tammuz, and men worshipping the sun. Each scene reveals greater abominations that drive the Lord from his own sanctuary.

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: Vision of idolatry inside Jerusalem's temple

chapters.title: The Mark upon the Faithful
chapters.synopsis: Six men with slaughter weapons are summoned, and a man clothed in linen with a writer's inkhorn marks the foreheads of all who sigh and cry over the abominations of Jerusalem. The destroyers slay the unmarked, beginning at the sanctuary, while Ezekiel pleads for the remnant.

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: The faithful marked; judgment begins at the sanctuary

chapters.title: Glory at the Threshold
chapters.synopsis: The man in linen scatters coals of fire from between the cherubim over the city. The glory of the Lord rises from the cherub and stands over the threshold of the house, and Ezekiel recognizes the living creatures of his first vision by the river Chebar.

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: Coals of fire; the glory moves toward departure

chapters.title: The Glory Departs the City
chapters.synopsis: Ezekiel prophesies against princes who devise mischief, and Pelatiah dies as he speaks. The Lord promises the scattered captives one heart and a new spirit, a heart of flesh in place of stone, and then his glory leaves the city as Ezekiel returns in vision to tell the exiles.

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: Judgment on the counsellors of the city

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: A new heart promised to the scattered

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: The glory departs; Ezekiel tells the captives

chapters.title: The Sign of the Exile's Baggage
chapters.synopsis: Ezekiel carries out his belongings by day and digs through the wall at evening as a sign that the prince and people of Jerusalem will go into captivity. The Lord answers those who say the vision is for far-off days: none of his words will be prolonged any more.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Acting out the removal into captivity

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The vision is for now, not distant days

chapters.title: Untempered Mortar of False Prophets
chapters.synopsis: The Lord condemns prophets who follow their own spirit and have seen nothing, daubing a flimsy wall with untempered mortar that will fall in the storm. Women who sew magic charms to hunt souls are likewise judged, for they have made the righteous sad and strengthened the wicked.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Woe to prophets who see false visions

chapters.title: Idols Set Up in the Heart
chapters.synopsis: Elders come to enquire of the Lord while cherishing idols in their hearts, and God refuses to be enquired of by them until they repent. Even if Noah, Daniel, and Job stood in a rebellious land, they would deliver only their own souls by their righteousness.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Repent of heart-idols; the righteous save themselves only

chapters.title: The Vine Fit for Fire
chapters.synopsis: The Lord compares Jerusalem to the wood of a wild vine, useless for any work and good only for fuel. Burned at both ends and charred in the middle, the city will pass from fire to fire because its people have trespassed.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Jerusalem as unprofitable vine wood

chapters.title: The Foundling Bride's Unfaithfulness
chapters.synopsis: In an extended allegory, the Lord recounts finding Jerusalem as an abandoned infant, raising her, entering covenant with her, and adorning her as a bride, only to have her trust in her own beauty and play the harlot with every passing nation. Though she has done worse than Samaria and Sodom, the Lord will remember his covenant and establish it with her forever, that she may be ashamed and know that he is God.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The foundling bride turned unfaithful

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Worse than Samaria and Sodom

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: An everlasting covenant remembered

chapters.title: Riddle of the Two Eagles
chapters.synopsis: A great eagle crops the top of a cedar and plants a vine that bends its roots toward a second eagle, a riddle of Judah's king breaking his oath to Babylon by turning to Egypt. The Lord vows the covenant-breaker will die in Babylon, then promises to plant a tender twig upon a high mountain of Israel, a kingdom under which all fowl shall dwell.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The eagles, the vine, and the broken oath

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: A tender twig planted on a high mountain

chapters.title: The Soul That Sinneth Shall Die
chapters.synopsis: The Lord repudiates the proverb that children's teeth are set on edge by their fathers' sour grapes: every soul answers for its own conduct. The wicked who turn from sin will live and their transgressions will not be mentioned, for God has no pleasure in the death of him that dieth, and pleads, turn yourselves, and live.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Individual accountability; turn and live

chapters.title: Lamentation for the Princes
chapters.synopsis: Ezekiel raises a lament for the princes of Israel as lion whelps caught and carried to Egypt and Babylon. The mother, once a fruitful vine, is plucked up and planted in the wilderness, with no strong rod left to be a sceptre to rule.

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: Lament for captive lion whelps and the vine

chapters.title: Rebellions Rehearsed, Gathering Promised
chapters.synopsis: When elders come to enquire, the Lord rehearses Israel's rebellions from Egypt through the wilderness to the present, sparing them each time for his name's sake. He vows to rule them with a mighty hand, purge out the rebels, and gather them from the countries to serve him on his holy mountain.

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: Elders come to enquire of the Lord

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Israel's history of rebellion; future gathering

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: A fire kindled in the south

chapters.title: The Sword of the Lord Drawn
chapters.synopsis: The Lord draws his sword from its sheath against Jerusalem, sharpened and furbished for the slaughter, and Ezekiel is commanded to sigh and cry. The wicked prince is told to remove the diadem: the kingdom will be overturned, overturned, overturned, until he comes whose right it is, and God will give it him.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The sword unsheathed; the crown removed until Messiah

chapters.title: The Sins of the Bloody City
chapters.synopsis: The Lord catalogues Jerusalem's sins: blood, extortion, profaned holy things, princes like wolves, and prophets daubing with untempered mortar. Israel has become dross to be melted in the furnace, and God sought for a man to stand in the gap before him for the land, but found none.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Jerusalem's sins; none to stand in the gap

chapters.title: Aholah and Aholibah
chapters.synopsis: Two sisters, Aholah and Aholibah, figure Samaria and Jerusalem, who gave themselves to the idolatries and alliances of Assyria, Babylon, and Egypt. Their lovers become their destroyers, and their judgment warns all who forget the Lord and follow after strange gods.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The two sisters and their unfaithfulness

chapters.title: The Boiling Pot and the Silent Mourner
chapters.synopsis: On the very day Babylon lays siege to Jerusalem, the Lord gives the parable of a rusted pot boiling over the fire, whose scum will not go out until it is consumed. Ezekiel's wife, the desire of his eyes, dies, and he is forbidden to mourn as a sign that the exiles will not mourn when the sanctuary is profaned.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Parable of the boiling pot as the siege begins

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: Ezekiel's wife dies; mourning forbidden as a sign

chapters.title: Judgments on Neighboring Nations
chapters.synopsis: Because Ammon, Moab, Edom, and Philistia rejoiced over Judah's calamity or took revenge upon her, the Lord pronounces judgment on each in turn. The nations that mocked the sanctuary will themselves know that he is the Lord.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Against Ammon, Moab, Edom, and Philistia

chapters.title: Tyre Beneath the Waves of Nations
chapters.synopsis: Because Tyre gloated that Jerusalem's fall would enrich her, the Lord will bring many nations against her like the sea casting up its waves. Nebuchadnezzar will break her towers, her stones and timber will be laid in the midst of the water, and she will be a place to spread nets.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Many nations against Tyre like the sea

chapters.title: Lament for the Ship of Tyre
chapters.synopsis: Ezekiel raises a lamentation over Tyre as a splendid merchant ship built of the finest materials, manned and stocked by all the trading peoples of the earth. Broken by the east wind in the heart of the seas, her riches and mariners sink, and the merchants of the nations hiss at her end.

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: Lamentation for Tyre, the wrecked merchant ship

chapters.title: The Fall of the Proud King
chapters.synopsis: The prince of Tyre, whose heart is lifted up to say I am a God, will die the death of the uncircumcised at the hand of strangers. A lament over the king of Tyre pictures an anointed covering cherub, perfect until iniquity was found in him and pride cast him down; Zidon too is judged, while Israel is promised safe dwelling.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The prince and king of Tyre brought down

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Against Zidon; Israel to dwell safely

chapters.title: The Great Dragon of Egypt
chapters.synopsis: The Lord is against Pharaoh, the great dragon lying in his rivers who says the river is his own. Egypt will be desolate forty years and afterward remain a base kingdom, and the land is given to Nebuchadnezzar as wages for his long service against Tyre.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Against Pharaoh, the dragon of the rivers

chapters.title: The Day of Egypt's Clouds
chapters.synopsis: Ezekiel wails for the day of the Lord that comes upon Egypt and her allies: her cities will fall, her idols cease from Noph, and her pride of power come down. The Lord breaks Pharaoh's arms and strengthens the arms of the king of Babylon.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The day of the Lord upon Egypt

chapters.title: The Cedar Felled in Lebanon
chapters.synopsis: Egypt is warned by the fate of Assyria, once a cedar in Lebanon whose top reached the clouds and sheltered all nations, until its heart was lifted up in its height. Delivered to the mighty one of the heathen, it was cut down, that no trees exalt themselves for their height.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Assyria the fallen cedar, a warning to Egypt

chapters.title: Pharaoh Laid Among the Slain
chapters.synopsis: Ezekiel laments for Pharaoh as a whale thrashing in the seas, caught in the Lord's net while the heavens are darkened over him. Egypt descends to the pit to lie with Asshur, Elam, Meshech, Edom, and all the multitudes slain by the sword.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Lament for Pharaoh; the nations in the pit

chapters.title: The Watchman and the Fallen City
chapters.synopsis: The Lord renews Ezekiel's calling as watchman: if he warns, the blood is on the hearers; if he is silent, it is on him, for God has no pleasure in the death of the wicked. A fugitive brings word that Jerusalem is smitten, Ezekiel's mouth is opened, and the people hear his words as a lovely song but will not do them.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The watchman's charge renewed; turn ye, why die

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: News of Jerusalem's fall; hearers who do not

chapters.title: Shepherds Judged, One Shepherd Promised
chapters.synopsis: The Lord indicts the shepherds of Israel who feed themselves and not the flock, leaving the sheep scattered on every mountain. He himself will search out his sheep, gather them, and feed them in good pasture, setting up one shepherd, his servant David, and making with them a covenant of peace.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: False shepherds judged; the Lord gathers his flock

chapters.title: Judgment upon Mount Seir
chapters.synopsis: Because Edom nursed a perpetual hatred and shed the blood of Israel in the time of calamity, saying the two nations shall be mine, the Lord makes Mount Seir a perpetual desolation. As Edom rejoiced over Israel's inheritance, so all the earth will rejoice at Edom's fall.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Mount Seir desolate for hatred of Israel

chapters.title: A New Heart and a New Spirit
chapters.synopsis: The mountains of Israel, long mocked by the heathen, will shoot forth branches and bear fruit for the returning people. For his holy name's sake the Lord will gather Israel, sprinkle clean water upon them, give them a heart of flesh and his own Spirit, and make the waste land like the garden of Eden.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The mountains of Israel made fruitful again

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: A new heart and spirit for the gathered

chapters.title: Dry Bones and the Two Sticks
chapters.synopsis: In a valley full of dry bones Ezekiel prophesies, and bone comes to bone, flesh and breath return, and an exceeding great army stands, a promise that the whole house of Israel will be raised from its graves and gathered home. He then joins the stick of Judah and the stick of Joseph into one, a latter-day prophecy that the Bible and the Book of Mormon would become one witness in the Lord's hand as Israel is gathered under one shepherd with a sanctuary in their midst for evermore.

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: The valley of dry bones lives

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Sticks of Judah and Joseph become one

chapters.title: Gog Comes Against the Gathered
chapters.synopsis: In the latter years Gog of the land of Magog leads a vast confederacy against Israel, gathered out of the nations and dwelling safely in unwalled villages. The Lord himself brings Gog forth so that he may be sanctified before all nations, and his fury rises with earthquake, pestilence, and great hailstones.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Gog's latter-day assault on gathered Israel

chapters.title: The Fall of Gog and Israel's Cleansing
chapters.synopsis: Gog's armies fall upon the mountains of Israel; their weapons fuel fires for seven years, and seven months are spent burying them in the valley of Hamon-gog. The heathen learn that Israel went captive for iniquity, and the Lord gathers his people, hiding his face no more, having poured out his Spirit upon the house of Israel.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Gog destroyed; the Spirit poured on Israel

chapters.title: The Man with the Measuring Reed
chapters.synopsis: In the twenty-fifth year of captivity Ezekiel is carried in vision to a very high mountain in Israel, where a man whose appearance is like brass stands with a line of flax and a measuring reed. Gate by gate and court by court, the messenger measures a future temple and charges Ezekiel to declare all he sees to the house of Israel.

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: Carried to a high mountain; the measurer appears

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: Gates and courts of the temple measured

chapters.title: Measuring the Holy House
chapters.synopsis: The man measures the temple itself: the porch, the holy place, and the most holy place, with its side chambers, palm trees, and cherubim carved on the walls. Every wall, door, and ornament is recorded, down to the altar of wood that is the table before the Lord.

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: The sanctuary and most holy place measured

chapters.title: Chambers for the Priests
chapters.synopsis: Ezekiel is shown the chambers north and south of the separate place, holy rooms where the priests who approach the Lord eat the most holy things and lay their garments. The outer wall, five hundred reeds on every side, makes a separation between the sanctuary and the profane place.

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: Holy chambers and the wall of separation

chapters.title: The Glory Fills the House
chapters.synopsis: The glory of the God of Israel comes from the way of the east, the same vision Ezekiel saw by the river Chebar, and fills the house as a voice declares this the place of his throne, where he will dwell in the midst of Israel for ever. Ezekiel is told to show the house to Israel that they may be ashamed of their iniquities, and the altar and its dedication offerings are described.

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: The glory returns and fills the temple

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The altar and its consecration

chapters.title: The Shut Gate and the Priests
chapters.synopsis: The east gate is shut because the Lord, the God of Israel, has entered by it. No stranger uncircumcised in heart may enter the sanctuary; the Levites who went astray bear their shame in lesser service, while the sons of Zadok who kept the charge stand to minister before the Lord under strict laws of dress, conduct, and inheritance.

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: The shut east gate; ordinances for the priests

chapters.title: The Holy Portion of the Land
chapters.synopsis: When the land is divided, an oblation is set apart for the sanctuary, the priests, the Levites, the city, and the prince. Princes are commanded to remove violence and use just balances, and the offerings and feasts, including the passover, are appointed to make reconciliation for the house of Israel.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The oblation of land; just princes; appointed feasts

chapters.title: Worship at the Temple Gates
chapters.synopsis: The gate toward the east is opened on sabbaths and new moons, and the prince and the people of the land worship at its threshold, entering and leaving by opposite gates. Rules govern the prince's offerings and inheritance, and Ezekiel is shown the courts where the ministers boil the sacrifices of the people.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Sabbath worship; offerings; the boiling places

chapters.title: Waters Issuing from the Sanctuary
chapters.synopsis: Waters issue from under the threshold of the house, rising from ankles to knees to loins to a river that cannot be passed over. Everything lives whither the river comes: the sea is healed, fishers spread nets from En-gedi, and trees on both banks bear monthly fruit with leaves for medicine; then the borders of the land to be inherited are set forth.

segments.speaker: ezekiel
segments.note: The healing river deepens from the temple

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The borders of the inheritance

chapters.title: The Lord Is There
chapters.synopsis: The land is divided in parallel portions among the twelve tribes, with the holy oblation, the sanctuary, and the city in their midst. The city's twelve gates bear the names of the tribes of Israel, and its name from that day shall be, The Lord is there.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The tribes' portions; the city named for the Lord
